newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber futures easier in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber futures easier in thin trade.

text.p: Rubber futures were slightly easier by midday on Thursday in very thin trade with most players poised to go on their vacations for the Christmas holiday period, dealers said.

"The only thing done this morning was in the ring sessions for 25 tonnes of January RSS3 rubber. The shortcovering we saw early this week may be fading away as we get closer to the holidays," a local rubber trader said.
Dealers said the market will probably become very quiet especially on Monday when Japan celebrates Emperor Akihito's birthday and on Christmas Day when markets shut down.
"It's going to be very difficult to conduct any business next week because nobody will be around," another dealer said.
At around 0445 GMT, January RSS3 was seen at 124.00-125.00 U.S. cents a kg compared with the previous 124.50 cents.
February RSS1 was indicated at 177.00-179.00 Singapore cents (US$1.26-$1.28) a kg against 179.25 cents.
February TSR20 was indicated at 171.75 Singapore cents (US$1.23) a kg from 172.75 cents.
